clues.original_explanation: Honey pours smooth and a mirror is the smoothest surface in the house.
clues.criticism: Generic. A shared adjective, applied separately, that would fit a hundred pairs.

clues.original_explanation: Honey is gold in the jar and an old mirror sits in a gilt frame.
clues.criticism: Colour padding again; a gilt frame and a jar of honey have nothing in common but a hue.

clues.original_explanation: Honey goes into a face mask and the mirror is where the result gets inspected.
clues.criticism: The explanation builds a small scene - face mask, then inspection - to manufacture a link that is not in the clue.

clues.original_explanation: The honeymoon follows the wedding and is named for the moon-month of sweetness after it.
clues.criticism: The honeymoon follows the wedding; one compound, both words.

clues.original_explanation: Honey is golden and a harvest moon hangs gold on the horizon.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. A harvest moon and a jar of honey share a hue and nothing else.

clues.original_explanation: Moon is the old root of month, and the honeymoon was originally the first month of marriage.
clues.criticism: Moon is the old root of month and the honeymoon was the first month of marriage; real etymology.

clues.original_explanation: Bees work the roses and honey is what comes of it.
clues.criticism: Bees work the roses and honey is what comes of it; straightforward cause and effect.

clues.original_explanation: A rose holds nectar and nectar is what becomes honey.
clues.criticism: A rose holds nectar and nectar becomes honey; literal.

clues.original_explanation: Honey is sweet and a rose is the sweetest thing in the garden to smell.
clues.criticism: Honey is sweet and a rose is the sweetest thing in the garden to smell; two senses of sweet, fairly used.

clues.original_explanation: Honey is sweetness itself and salt is its exact opposite on the tongue.
clues.criticism: Honey is sweetness itself and salt is its opposite on the tongue; a clean contrast.

clues.original_explanation: Salt cures meat and honey is the other preservative that never spoils.
clues.criticism: Salt cures meat and honey is the other preservative that never spoils; a genuine shared property.

clues.original_explanation: Salt and sweet are two of the basic tastes and honey is the sweet one.
clues.criticism: Generic, and it repeats SWEET. Naming the basic tastes is a category, not a connection.

clues.original_explanation: Dark honey is the strong-tasting kind and a shadow is a patch of dark.
clues.criticism: Generic. Dark honey is a real product but a shadow being dark is the emptiest possible half of a clue.

clues.original_explanation: The sun makes the flowers the bees need for honey and the sun is also what makes shadows.
clues.criticism: Generic. The sun grows the flowers and the sun makes shadows: two separate facts about the sun, not a connection between HONEY and SHADOW.

clues.original_explanation: Honey is warm gold and shadow is the absence of exactly that.
clues.criticism: Colour padding dressed as contrast; warm gold against absence of gold is a mood, not a link.

clues.original_explanation: Honeyed words come off the tongue and a forked tongue is what a snake is trusted with; both describe sweet talk you should not believe.
clues.criticism: Honeyed words and a forked tongue; both describe sweet talk you should not believe.

clues.original_explanation: A honeytrap is something sweet with a snake inside it.
clues.criticism: A honeytrap is solid; the snake inside it is something the explanation adds rather than something TRAP evokes.

clues.original_explanation: A snake charmer does the charming and honeyed charm is how a smooth talker works.
clues.criticism: A snake charmer and honeyed charm; the word does real work on both sides.

clues.original_explanation: Bees come out in spring and the honey follows.
clues.criticism: Bees come out in spring and the honey follows.

clues.original_explanation: Spring blossom is the source of the nectar that becomes honey.
clues.criticism: Spring blossom is the source of the nectar that becomes honey.

clues.original_explanation: Spring is pollen season and pollen is what bees carry home alongside the nectar.
clues.criticism: Spring is pollen season and pollen is what bees carry home; literal.

clues.original_explanation: A horseshoe is a bent bar of iron.
clues.criticism: A horseshoe is a bent bar of iron; about as direct as clues get.

clues.original_explanation: The blacksmith works iron and shoes the horses.
clues.criticism: The blacksmith works iron and shoes the horses; one trade, both words.

clues.original_explanation: The iron horse was what they called the steam train when it first appeared.
clues.criticism: Both halves come from the same compound, the iron horse, which makes it slightly circular but still fair.

clues.original_explanation: A horse bolts across the field and a bolt is the lock a key throws.
clues.criticism: A horse bolts and a bolt is what a key throws; two unrelated senses that both land.

clues.original_explanation: The stable holds the horses and the key hangs by its door.
clues.criticism: The key hanging by the stable door is set dressing. The proverb about locking the stable door after the horse has bolted is the real clue and it is not used.

clues.original_explanation: Locking the gate after the horse has bolted is the proverb about acting too late.
clues.criticism: Locking the gate after the horse has bolted is a real proverb about acting too late.

clues.original_explanation: A dark horse is the unexpected winner and dark is the opposite of light.
clues.criticism: A dark horse is a fixed compound and dark is light's opposite; unlike the other DARK clues, both halves are earned.

clues.original_explanation: Light horse is the historical name for light cavalry.
clues.criticism: Light horse is the historical name for light cavalry; a real military term.

clues.original_explanation: Light travels at the fastest speed there is and a horse is judged on nothing but speed.
clues.criticism: The speed of light is a specific thing and a horse is judged on nothing else; loose but fair.

clues.original_explanation: You groom a horse in the stable and you groom yourself in the mirror.
clues.criticism: You groom a horse and groom yourself in the mirror; the same verb, two settings.

clues.original_explanation: A horse shies from its own reflection because it does not know what a mirror is.
clues.criticism: A horse shies from its own reflection because it does not know what a mirror is; cause and effect.

clues.original_explanation: The knight in chess is a horse and the White Knight rides through the looking-glass.
clues.criticism: The chess knight is a horse and the White Knight rides through the looking-glass; two real references.

clues.original_explanation: A mare is a female horse, and the dark plains on the moon are called maria, from mare.
clues.criticism: A mare is a female horse and the moon's dark plains are the maria; a genuine and satisfying overlap.

clues.original_explanation: A horseshoe is a crescent, which is exactly the shape of the moon in its thin phase.
clues.criticism: A horseshoe is a crescent, which is a shape the moon takes; visual but thin.

clues.original_explanation: A white horse and a white moon are both stock images.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. A white horse and a white moon are stock images joined by nothing.

clues.original_explanation: The Kentucky Derby is a horse race known as the Run for the Roses.
clues.criticism: The Kentucky Derby is the Run for the Roses; one race holds both words.

clues.original_explanation: The winning horse is draped in a blanket of roses.
clues.criticism: The winning horse is draped in a blanket of roses; a real and specific object.

clues.original_explanation: A rider rises to the trot and rose is the past tense of rise.
clues.criticism: A rider rising to the trot is technical horsemanship; the rose-as-past-tense pun is doing all the work and it appears in four pairs.

clues.original_explanation: A salt lick is the block put out in the field for horses.
clues.criticism: A salt lick is the block put out in the field for horses; one object, both words.

clues.original_explanation: A worked horse sweats and dries white with salt.
clues.criticism: A worked horse dries white with salt; literal and vivid.

clues.original_explanation: You can lead a horse to water but not make it drink, and salt water is the kind nothing can drink.
clues.criticism: The proverb is strong on HORSE; salt water is a second, separate idea about a different water.

clues.original_explanation: A horse shies at its own shadow on the road.
clues.criticism: A horse shies at its own shadow on the road; a real and specific behaviour.

clues.original_explanation: A shadow is exactly what spooks a horse.
clues.criticism: A shadow is exactly what spooks a horse; the same idea as SHY, told plainly.

clues.original_explanation: The rider's shadow is thrown along the ground beside the horse.
clues.criticism: The rider's shadow on the ground is scenery; any moving thing has one.

clues.original_explanation: Antivenom for snake bites is produced in horses, which are injected to make the serum.
clues.criticism: Antivenom really is produced in horses, but that is specialist knowledge the explanation has to supply.

clues.original_explanation: A startled horse rears up and so does a cobra.
clues.criticism: A startled horse rears and so does a cobra; the same motion, two animals.

clues.original_explanation: A horse is known for its tail and a snake is very nearly all tail.
clues.criticism: A horse's tail is a feature; saying a snake is nearly all tail is a joke, not a connection.

clues.original_explanation: The Derby is the great horse race and it is run in spring.
clues.criticism: The great races are run in spring; fair, though DERBY is stronger in the ROSE pair.

clues.original_explanation: Foals are born in spring.
clues.criticism: Foals are born in spring; simple and literal.

clues.original_explanation: A horse jumps the fence and to spring is to jump.
clues.criticism: A horse jumps the fence and to spring is to jump; the verb sense carries it.

clues.original_explanation: A heavy iron lock is what an old key was cut for.
clues.criticism: Lock and key is fixed; the iron half is just what the old lock was made of.

clues.original_explanation: A locksmith cuts keys and a blacksmith works iron.
clues.criticism: A locksmith cuts keys and a blacksmith works iron; one suffix, two trades.

clues.original_explanation: A key is a small piece of shaped metal and iron is what the old ones were cast from.
clues.criticism: Generic category padding: it says only that both are made of metal.

clues.original_explanation: Cast iron is the material and light is cast across a room.
clues.criticism: Cast iron is the material and light is cast across a room; two real uses of one verb.

clues.original_explanation: Iron is the byword for heavy and light is its exact opposite.
clues.criticism: Iron is the byword for heavy and light is its exact opposite; the contrast is clean.

clues.original_explanation: Polished iron shines when the light hits it.
clues.criticism: Polished iron shining is true of any polished metal; the iron half is not specific.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror is polished to a shine and iron is polished to keep the rust off.
clues.criticism: Both are polished, which is thin, but rust prevention and reflection are at least different reasons.

clues.original_explanation: Polished iron shines enough to see yourself in, which is how the first mirrors worked.
clues.criticism: Polished iron was how the first mirrors worked; genuinely educational.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror hangs in a wrought iron frame.
clues.criticism: A mirror in a wrought iron frame; co-location, but a very common one.

clues.original_explanation: The man in the moon and Iron Man are both familiar figures.
clues.criticism: The man in the moon and Iron Man; two familiar figures sharing one word.

clues.original_explanation: The moon's surface and raw iron are both grey.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. Raw iron and the moon's surface are both grey, and so is a great deal else.

clues.original_explanation: The moon has a small iron core, and iron is the metal we associate with a planet's core.
clues.criticism: The moon has a small iron core; a real fact that joins the two words directly.

clues.original_explanation: A wrought iron gate with roses climbing over it is the standard garden picture.
clues.criticism: A wrought iron gate with roses over it is the standard garden picture; co-location, but a vivid one.

clues.original_explanation: Rust is the deep red-brown of old iron and roses come in exactly that colour.
clues.criticism: Rust as a rose colour is a stretch, and RUST is already used in five pairs.

clues.original_explanation: The rose garden is full of wrought iron benches and arches.
clues.criticism: The rose garden is strong; the ironwork in it is furniture.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is what makes iron rust.
clues.criticism: Salt is what makes iron rust; a direct causal fact.

clues.original_explanation: Iron and salt are both minerals a body needs.
clues.criticism: Iron and salt are both minerals a body needs; a real shared category rather than a vague one.

clues.original_explanation: Sea salt eats iron, which is why ships are a losing battle.
clues.criticism: Sea salt eats iron, which is why ships are a losing battle; overlaps RUST.

clues.original_explanation: The Iron Curtain is always described as having cast a shadow over half of Europe.
clues.criticism: The Iron Curtain is always described as casting a shadow over half of Europe; the phrase itself carries both.

clues.original_explanation: Iron bars throw striped shadows across a cell floor.
clues.criticism: Iron bars throwing striped shadows on a cell floor is a real image, if the shadow half is only geometry.

clues.original_explanation: Raw iron is dark grey and a shadow is a patch of dark.
clues.criticism: Generic. Raw iron being dark grey and a shadow being dark share an adjective and nothing else.

clues.original_explanation: A snake coils and iron is coiled into wire and springs.
clues.criticism: A snake coils; iron coiled into wire is true but is not what COIL evokes.

clues.original_explanation: An iron rod is a bar of metal and Moses' rod turned into a snake in front of Pharaoh.
clues.criticism: Moses' rod turning into a serpent is a genuine story, though the explanation has to name it.

clues.original_explanation: A snake is covered in scales and the flaky crust on hot iron is called mill scale.
clues.criticism: Mill scale on hot iron is metallurgical trade vocabulary; no player will ever reach it.

clues.original_explanation: A spring is a coil of iron wire.
clues.criticism: A spring is a coil of iron wire; literal on both sides.

clues.original_explanation: Springs are made of steel, which is iron with the carbon adjusted.
clues.criticism: Springs are steel, which is iron with the carbon adjusted; accurate and connecting.

clues.original_explanation: A mattress is filled with iron springs.
clues.criticism: A mattress full of springs is strong on SPRING; the iron is incidental.

clues.original_explanation: You turn on a light and you turn a key.
clues.criticism: You turn on a light and you turn a key; two uses of one common verb, but both are natural. TURN is used in four pairs.

clues.original_explanation: The ignition key is turned and the dashboard lights come on.
clues.criticism: The ignition key is turned and the dashboard lights come on; a real sequence.

clues.original_explanation: In photography the key light is the main lamp lighting the subject.
clues.criticism: The key light is genuinely the main lamp in a photographic set-up; specialist but exact.

clues.original_explanation: A car needs a key to start and has mirrors to drive.
clues.criticism: A car needs a key and has mirrors; co-location, but unarguable.

clues.original_explanation: A key is copied at the shop and a mirror copies whatever stands in front of it.
clues.criticism: A key is copied at the shop; a mirror copying whatever stands in front of it is a metaphor the explanation supplies.

clues.original_explanation: The hall mirror hangs above the table where the keys are dropped.
clues.criticism: A hall table with a mirror above it and keys on it is furniture arrangement, not a connection.

clues.original_explanation: The Moonlight Sonata is a piano piece and a piano is played with keys.
clues.criticism: The Moonlight Sonata is a piano piece and a piano is played with keys.

clues.original_explanation: Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata is written in a musical key, C sharp minor.
clues.criticism: The same reference as PIANO, reached by a narrower route.

clues.original_explanation: A key turns in a lock and the moon turns through its phases.
clues.criticism: A key turns in a lock and the moon turns through its phases; two unrelated uses of one over-used clue.

clues.original_explanation: In The Secret Garden a buried key unlocks the walled garden full of roses.
clues.criticism: In The Secret Garden a buried key unlocks the walled garden full of roses; one story, both words.

clues.original_explanation: You press a key and you press a rose flat between the pages of a book.
clues.criticism: You press a key and you press a rose flat between pages; two real uses of one verb.

clues.original_explanation: The Rose is a famous song and every song is written in a key.
clues.criticism: The Rose is a song most players will not have; every song being in a key is generic music.

clues.original_explanation: A key is a low-lying island and salt water is what surrounds one.
clues.criticism: A key is a low-lying island and salt water is what surrounds one.

clues.original_explanation: The Florida Keys are a chain of islands sitting in salt water.
clues.criticism: The Florida Keys sit in salt water; a specific, recognisable place.

clues.original_explanation: The sea is salt and a key is an island standing in it.
clues.criticism: The same idea as ISLAND, with the key half weaker.

clues.original_explanation: A skeleton key opens any lock and a skeleton is the shape a shadow makes of a person.
clues.criticism: A skeleton key is instant; 'a skeleton is the shape a shadow makes of a person' is an invention of the explanation.

clues.original_explanation: A key opens the door and the shadow under it is what tells you someone is standing there.
clues.criticism: The shadow under a door telling you someone is standing there is a genuine and specific image.

clues.original_explanation: A key turns in the lock and a shadow turns as the sun moves.
clues.criticism: A key turning and a shadow turning with the sun are unconnected; TURN is doing duty in four pairs.

clues.original_explanation: A snake charmer plays a flute and a flute is worked with keys.
clues.criticism: A snake charmer plays a flute and a flute is worked with keys; one instrument, both words.

clues.original_explanation: A snake coils and a keyring is a coil of split wire.
clues.criticism: A keyring being a coil of split wire is a technicality; COIL points at the snake.

clues.original_explanation: A snake charmer does the charming and a charm is what hangs off a keyring.
clues.criticism: The snake charmer is strong; a charm on a keyring is a weak second half.

clues.original_explanation: You wind a clockwork spring using a key.
clues.criticism: You wind a clockwork spring using a key; one action holds both words.

clues.original_explanation: A clock is driven by a spring and wound with a key.
clues.criticism: A clock is driven by a spring and wound with a key.

clues.original_explanation: A lock is a spring-loaded mechanism and a key is what releases it.
clues.criticism: A lock is a spring-loaded mechanism and a key is what releases it; genuinely mechanical.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror exists to reflect light.
clues.criticism: A mirror exists to reflect light. REFLECT is over-used across the set, but this is the one pair where it is exactly right.

clues.original_explanation: A beam of light is what bounces off a mirror.
clues.criticism: A beam of light is what bounces off a mirror; literal optics.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror throws glare the moment light catches it.
clues.criticism: A mirror throws glare the moment light catches it.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror is backed with silver precisely because silver throws light back.
clues.criticism: A mirror is backed with silver precisely because silver throws light back; educational.

clues.original_explanation: The moon makes no light of its own; it only reflects the sun's.
clues.criticism: The moon makes no light of its own and only reflects the sun's; the single best fact in the whole set.

clues.original_explanation: The moon is pale and the light it casts is pale.
clues.criticism: Pale moonlight is a fixed description, so the adjective is earned here rather than padded.

clues.original_explanation: Both the moon and the light it throws are described as silver.
clues.criticism: Both the moon and the light it throws are described as silver; conventional but fair.

clues.original_explanation: The moon is the light source of the night sky.
clues.criticism: The moon is the light source of the night sky.

clues.original_explanation: Rosy-fingered dawn is the old description of the day's first light.
clues.criticism: Rosy-fingered dawn is the oldest description of the day's first light; one phrase, both words.

clues.original_explanation: Rose-tinted glasses change the colour of the light you see through them.
clues.criticism: Rose-tinted glasses change the colour of the light you see through them; a real object.

clues.original_explanation: A sunset is light at its reddest and rose is the colour it turns the sky.
clues.criticism: A sunset is light at its reddest and rose is the colour it turns the sky.

clues.original_explanation: A Himalayan salt lamp is a block of salt lit from the inside.
clues.criticism: A Himalayan salt lamp is a block of salt lit from inside; a single object holding both words.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is white and white light is the full spectrum.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. Salt being white and white light being the full spectrum are two unrelated facts.

clues.original_explanation: Salt forms crystals and crystals are what split light into colours.
clues.criticism: Salt forms crystals and crystals split light into colours; a real physical link.

clues.original_explanation: Light is what casts a shadow.
clues.criticism: Light is what casts a shadow; the most direct clue in the set.

clues.original_explanation: A shadow is a patch of dark and dark is what light is not.
clues.criticism: Unlike the other DARK clues this one is a true contrast: a shadow is where light is not.

clues.original_explanation: The sun is the light that puts shadows on the ground.
clues.criticism: The sun is the light that puts shadows on the ground.

clues.original_explanation: Shadow puppets work by putting a hand between a lamp and the screen.
clues.criticism: Shadow puppets work by putting a hand between a lamp and a screen; one craft, both words.

clues.original_explanation: A snake needs the sun, which is the light everything else runs on too.
clues.criticism: A snake needs the sun, which is true but reaches LIGHT only by the most general route.

clues.original_explanation: A snake basks in full light to warm itself.
clues.criticism: Basking is strongly snake; the light is only what it happens to bask in.

clues.original_explanation: A snake is covered in scales and scales are what tell you whether something is light or heavy.
clues.criticism: A snake is covered in scales and scales are what tell you if something is light or heavy; the homonym is genuinely funny.

clues.original_explanation: A light bulb and a spring bulb like a daffodil take exactly the same word.
clues.criticism: A light bulb and a spring bulb take exactly the same word; the best pure wordplay in the set.

clues.original_explanation: Spring is when the days lengthen and daylight is what lengthens.
clues.criticism: Spring is when the days lengthen and daylight is what lengthens.

clues.original_explanation: Dawn is first light and in spring it arrives earlier every morning.
clues.criticism: Repeats DAY; the spring half is only that dawn comes earlier.

clues.original_explanation: A mirror reflects, and the moon shines only by reflecting sunlight.
clues.criticism: True on both sides, but it is the ninth REFLECT clue and the mirror half is a definition rather than a puzzle.

clues.original_explanation: Mirrors are silvered glass and the moon is called silver.
clues.criticism: Mirrors are silvered glass and the moon is called silver; fair.

clues.original_explanation: You look for your face in a mirror, and the face of the moon is what we call its near side.
clues.criticism: You look for your face in a mirror and the face of the moon is what we call its near side; two real uses.

clues.original_explanation: In Beauty and the Beast the enchanted rose and the magic mirror are the two objects the whole story turns on.
clues.criticism: In Beauty and the Beast the enchanted rose and the magic mirror are the two objects the story turns on.

clues.original_explanation: Rose-tinted is how the glasses are described and a tinted mirror is the smoked kind.
clues.criticism: Rose-tinted is strong; a tinted mirror is a different and much weaker use of the word.

clues.original_explanation: A rose sits on the vanity table beside the mirror.
clues.criticism: A rose on the vanity table is decoration; the connection is proximity.

clues.original_explanation: Spilling salt and breaking a mirror are the two great pieces of bad luck.
clues.criticism: Spilling salt and breaking a mirror are the two great pieces of bad luck; one superstition, both words.

clues.original_explanation: Salt goes over your shoulder and a mirror is what you check over it.
clues.criticism: Salt goes over your shoulder and a mirror is what you check over it; the same gesture twice.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is a crystal and an old mirror is crystal glass.
clues.criticism: Calling an old mirror crystal glass is loose; salt being a crystal is exact. Uneven.

clues.original_explanation: A vampire casts no shadow and shows no reflection in a mirror.
clues.criticism: A vampire casts no shadow and shows no reflection; one creature defined by the absence of both.

clues.original_explanation: Your shadow and your reflection are both doubles of you that are not you.
clues.criticism: Your shadow and your reflection are both doubles of you that are not you.

clues.original_explanation: The shadow self and the face in the mirror are the two ways of meeting yourself.
clues.criticism: The shadow self and the face in the mirror are two ways of meeting yourself.

clues.original_explanation: Medusa had snakes for hair and Perseus killed her by watching her reflection in a polished shield.
clues.criticism: Medusa had snakes for hair and Perseus used a polished shield as a mirror; one myth, both words.

clues.original_explanation: The mirrored shield is the only way anyone ever got near the snake-haired Gorgon.
clues.criticism: The same myth as MEDUSA by a narrower route.

clues.original_explanation: A snake's unblinking stare and the one that comes back out of a mirror are equally hard to hold.
clues.criticism: A snake's unblinking stare is vivid; the stare coming back out of a mirror is your own, which is a different idea.

clues.original_explanation: A spring collects in a still pool that works as a mirror.
clues.criticism: A spring collects in a still pool that works as a mirror; physically true.

clues.original_explanation: Narcissus fell in love with his reflection in a spring, and narcissus is also the spring flower he became.
clues.criticism: Narcissus fell in love with his reflection in a spring and became the spring flower; a double connection in one word.

clues.original_explanation: The calm surface of a spring reflects exactly as a mirror does.
clues.criticism: REFLECT again. It repeats POOL and gives the MIRROR half away for nothing.

clues.original_explanation: The moon rises every night, and rose is the past tense of rise.
clues.criticism: The moon rises and rose is the past tense of rise; clean wordplay.

clues.original_explanation: Pale rose is a colour and a pale moon is the standard description.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. Pale rose is a paint chart and a pale moon is a cliche; nothing joins them.

clues.original_explanation: A moon garden is planted with pale flowers, roses among them, to be seen by moonlight.
clues.criticism: A moon garden is a real but specialist planting idea the explanation has to teach.

clues.original_explanation: Sea salt is where salt comes from, and the moon rules the sea through the tides.
clues.criticism: Sea salt is where salt comes from and the moon rules the sea through the tides.

clues.original_explanation: The moon pulls the tides, and the salt water they carry leaves salt flats behind.
clues.criticism: The moon pulls the tides and the salt water they carry leaves salt flats behind.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is white and so is the moon.
clues.criticism: Colour padding of the plainest kind.

clues.original_explanation: An eclipse is nothing but a shadow: the moon's on the earth, or the earth's on the moon.
clues.criticism: An eclipse is nothing but a shadow, the moon's or the earth's; exact and satisfying.

clues.original_explanation: The dark side of the moon is the famous phrase, and a shadow is a patch of dark.
clues.criticism: The dark side of the moon is a fixed phrase, which makes this DARK clue earn its place where most do not.

clues.original_explanation: The moon owns the night and moonlight is what casts shadows after dark.
clues.criticism: Moonlight is what casts shadows after dark.

clues.original_explanation: The moon's phases and a snake shedding its skin are both ancient symbols of renewal in cycles.
clues.criticism: The phases and the shedding are both renewal cycles, but the explanation has to state the symbolism for the clue to land.

clues.original_explanation: A crescent moon and a snake's body are both defined by their curve.
clues.criticism: A crescent moon and a snake's body are both defined by their curve; a visual link that holds.

clues.original_explanation: Many snakes hunt at night, which is when the moon is up.
clues.criticism: Some snakes hunt at night, which is a weak half against the moon's definitional one.

clues.original_explanation: The moon drives the tides, and a spring tide is the extra-high tide that arrives at full and new moon.
clues.criticism: A spring tide is a real named thing that arrives at full and new moon; the term itself joins both words.

clues.original_explanation: Easter falls on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring equinox.
clues.criticism: Easter falls on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring equinox; one rule, both words.

clues.original_explanation: Many cultures see a rabbit in the moon, and the rabbit is also the animal of spring and Easter.
clues.criticism: The rabbit in the moon and the rabbit of spring and Easter; two real traditions.

clues.original_explanation: A desert rose is a cluster of crystals that forms in salt flats and comes out shaped like a flower.
clues.criticism: A desert rose is a real crystal cluster that forms in salt flats and comes out flower-shaped.

clues.original_explanation: Salt water will kill a rose faster than anything else in the garden.
clues.criticism: Salt water will kill a rose faster than anything else in the garden; cause and effect.

clues.original_explanation: Salt preserves food and rose petals are preserved with salt to make potpourri.
clues.criticism: Salt preserves food and rose petals are salted for potpourri; a genuine shared method.

clues.original_explanation: Shade is another word for shadow and a rose will not flower in it.
clues.criticism: Shade is another word for shadow and a rose will not flower in it; the gardening fact does real work.

clues.original_explanation: The black rose is the gothic image and a shadow is black.
clues.criticism: Colour padding. The black rose is a gothic image and a shadow is dark; separately true, jointly nothing.

clues.original_explanation: At dusk the shadows stretch and the scent of roses gets stronger.
clues.criticism: Shadows stretching at dusk is exact; the scent of roses strengthening is a second, separate fact.

clues.original_explanation: A rose hides thorns and a snake hides in the grass; both are the danger you do not see coming.
clues.criticism: A rose's thorns are definitional; the snake half is the explanation's general point about unseen danger.

clues.original_explanation: The serpent was in the garden and the rose is what the garden is famous for.
clues.criticism: The serpent was in the garden and the rose is what a garden is famous for.

clues.original_explanation: A snake bites and a rose will draw blood too if you grab it wrong.
clues.criticism: A snake bites; a rose drawing blood is a thorn, which THORN already covers.

clues.original_explanation: Roses bloom when spring arrives.
clues.criticism: Roses bloom when spring arrives; simple and exact.

clues.original_explanation: A rosebud is the unopened flower and budding is what everything does in spring.
clues.criticism: A rosebud is the unopened flower and budding is what everything does in spring.

clues.original_explanation: The spring garden is where the roses are.
clues.criticism: The spring garden is where the roses are; true, but GARDEN is carrying six pairs.

clues.original_explanation: Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt and a pillar is a thing that throws a long shadow.
clues.criticism: Lot's wife as a pillar of salt is a strong reference, but 'a pillar throws a long shadow' is true of any upright object and the explanation has to add it.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is the whitest thing there is and a shadow is the darkest patch on the ground.
clues.criticism: Dressed as contrast, but it is still just salt being white and shadow being dark.

clues.original_explanation: Salt flats are desert and the desert is where shadows are sharpest.
clues.criticism: Salt flats are desert and desert shadows are the sharpest there are; the strongest of the three.

clues.original_explanation: The sea is salt and the sea snake lives in it.
clues.criticism: The sea is salt and the sea snake lives in it; literal.

clues.original_explanation: Rattlesnakes live out on the salt flats and desert.
clues.criticism: Rattlesnakes live out on salt flats and desert; true and specific.

clues.original_explanation: A snake is covered in scales and the crust salt leaves behind is also called scale.
clues.criticism: The crust salt leaves being called scale is industrial vocabulary no player has.

clues.original_explanation: Spring water and salt water are both bottled by the word that follows.
clues.criticism: Spring water and salt water; one word, two everyday compounds.

clues.original_explanation: A mineral spring is naturally salty water coming out of the ground.
clues.criticism: A mineral spring is naturally salty water coming out of the ground; a single real thing.

clues.original_explanation: Salt is thrown on roads to force the thaw that spring would bring anyway.
clues.criticism: Salt forces the thaw that spring would bring anyway; a nice piece of contrast.

clues.original_explanation: A snake lurks and so does a shadow.
clues.criticism: A snake lurks and so does a shadow; the verb is used the same way for both.

clues.original_explanation: A snake in the grass is the warning and the grass is where the shadows lie.
clues.criticism: A snake in the grass is instant; 'the grass is where the shadows lie' is the explanation inventing the other half.

clues.original_explanation: A snake strikes out of the shadows before you have seen it.
clues.criticism: Striking is snake; out of the shadows is atmosphere attached to it.

clues.original_explanation: If the groundhog sees its shadow there are six more weeks of winter, and if it does not, spring comes early.
clues.criticism: If the groundhog sees its shadow there are six more weeks of winter; one tradition, both words exactly.

clues.original_explanation: The returning spring sun is what starts casting real shadows again.
clues.criticism: The returning spring sun starts casting real shadows again; loose but true.

clues.original_explanation: Shadows shorten as spring moves the sun higher in the sky.
clues.criticism: Shadows shortening as the sun climbs is real; LENGTH is a dry word that points mostly at shadow.

clues.original_explanation: A spring is a coil and a snake coils.
clues.criticism: A spring is a coil and a snake coils; the cleanest possible double.

clues.original_explanation: Snakes wake from hibernation in spring.
clues.criticism: Snakes wake from hibernation in spring; literal and seasonal.

clues.original_explanation: A snake sheds its skin and spring is when the world sheds winter.
clues.criticism: A snake shedding is exact; 'spring sheds winter' is a poeticism the explanation supplies.
